voiceSample: My daughter's periods are all over the place. Is that normal at her age?
openingMessage: Are irregular periods normal at her age?
readyLine: Thank you. I have a good picture of what's going on for {name}. Tap below when you'd like my thoughts, or ask me anything first.
suggestedQuestions: When should we see a provider?

sections.title: What I'm Hearing
sections.body: {name}'s cycle hasn't settled into a steady rhythm yet, and you'd like to know whether that's part of growing up or something to look into.

sections.title: The Hypothalamic Connection
sections.body: In the first years after periods begin, the hypothalamus is still learning to time its signals to the ovaries. Sleep, stress, growth and nutrition all influence how quickly that rhythm settles.

sections.title: What This May Mean
sections.body: Irregular cycles are often part of the first few years. It may still be worth exploring with a provider if cycles are very far apart, very heavy, or come with pain that keeps her from her day.

sections.title: Questions for Your Provider
bullets: Is this pattern typical for how long she's been having periods?
Which signs would mean we should look further?
Could her sleep, stress or activity be playing a part?
What should we track before the next visit?

sections.title: Tests Worth Discussing
bullets: Whether any tests are useful yet, given her age.
Iron and ferritin if her periods are heavy.
A thyroid check if she's also tired or her weight has changed.

sections.title: What You Can Do Now
sections.body: Gentle foundations help a young hypothalamus find its rhythm:
bullets: A steady bedtime, even on weekends.
A simple cycle diary she keeps herself.

sections.title: A Word from Deborah
sections.body: Thank you for paying attention. Talking openly about cycles at this age helps {name} learn to listen to her own body — that's a gift for life.

answer.closingLine: Bring this to your provider. I help you ask better questions — your provider makes clinical decisions.
answer.summary: Irregular cycles in the first years after periods began.

followUps.reply: If cycles are more than three months apart, very heavy, or painful enough that she misses school, that's a good time to book a visit.
The first day of each period, how heavy it is, and how she feels. A few weeks of notes makes a provider visit much more useful.

fallbackReply: Thank you. Tell me as much as you'd like about how things are for {name}.
